## Motivation DSpark draft generation and verification on Ascend can benefit from dedicated NPU implementations of projection/add/argmax, temperature softmax, and draft acceptance. This PR connects SGLang to the corresponding `sgl-kernel-npu` APIs and selects NPU implementations using actual tensor placement, including environments where `transfer_to_npu` aliases CUDA device checks. Companion kernel PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/899. ## Modifications - Route `MarkovGreedyStep` to the NPU implementation with native projection and dtype-correct addition before token selection. - Route FP32 row argmax and DSpark greedy verification through the NPU argmax implementation. - Dispatch temperature softmax and the shared DFlash/DSpark accepted-prefix and bonus-token calculation to dedicated NPU kernels. - Add NPU dispatch tests covering device selection, numerical behavior, and integration boundaries. `MarkovSampleStep` dispatch changes are excluded from the current diff.

End-to-end accuracy: reference integration

The companion PR reports the following matched GPQA Diamond results:

Metric | Baseline | Integration -- | -- | -- Correct answers | 180/198 | 178/198 Accuracy | 91.37% | 90.36% API errors in the matched cohort | 0 | 0

The counts follow the reported overlap: 175 correct in both variants, five correct only in the baseline, and three correct only in the integration.

Speed Tests and Profiling

Single-operator performance

A3 graph-replay amortized latency reported by the companion PR; compilation and warmup excluded. Logit vocabulary size: 129280.

Operator / workload | Torch native (µs) | NPU implementation (µs) | Speedup -- | -- | -- | -- Markov greedy: B=64, R=64, FP32 base + BF16 projection | 89.98 | 79.43 | 1.13× Row argmax: 576 FP32 rows | 296.87 | 243.16 | 1.22× Temperature softmax: B=64, 9 rows/request, FP32 | 1338.39 | 1153.50 | 1.16× Accepted-prefix length + bonus: B=64, block length 9 | 94.28 | 12.80 | 7.37×

End-to-end serving: reference integration

Both variants ran in the same container on the same A3 host using:

  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8, ModelSlim W8A8, BF16 KV cache.
  • Non-quantized draft model; DSpark draft block size 6, verify length 7.
  • NPU graphs enabled; Radix cache disabled.
  • use_index_cache=true, index_topk_freq=4.
  • 128 input tokens, 1024 output tokens, concurrency 128; fixed corpus and seed 1, ignore_eos enabled.

Second-round warmed results:

Temperature | Metric | Baseline | Integration | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 0 | Output throughput (tokens/s) | 4671.52 | 4929.38 | +5.52% 0 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 18.60 | 18.94 | +1.86% 1 | Output throughput (tokens/s) | 3610.44 | 4286.05 | +18.71% 1 | Mean TPOT (ms) | 25.86 | 21.94 | −15.16% 1 | P99 TPOT (ms) | 33.20 | 28.23 | −14.97%

The baseline required a precision-fixed NPU Philox sampler because unmodified main failed graph capture on the tested stack. The measured integration additionally included Markov sampling dispatch and precomputed noise.

These measurements describe that reference integration; they do not isolate the four operator integrations retained in this PR.

Pending follow-up: repeat the controlled serving benchmark on the current revision before claiming these end-to-end gains for this PR.

## Checklist - [ ] Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add or update unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation where needed. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results where applicable. - [ ] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #40866183068](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40866183068) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #40866183125](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40866183125) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #40866182976](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40866182976)

+"""Numerical coverage for DSpark's SGLang-to-NPU dispatch boundary."""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+from torch_npu.contrib import transfer_to_npu  # noqa: F401
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.dispatch import inputs_on_cuda
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.dspark_accept import (
+    AcceptGreedy,
+    SoftmaxTemp,
+    _row_argmax,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.dspark_draft_model import MarkovGreedyStep
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.dspark_verify_window import (
+    BuildOutTokens,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_npu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_npu_ci(est_time=90, suite="base-b-test-1-npu-a3")
+
+
+class TestDSparkNpuDispatch(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+
+    def test_build_out_tokens_matches_full_torch_buffer(self):
+        from sgl_kernel_npu.operators import sample
+
+        for bs, gamma in ((0, 7), (1, 0), (33, 7)):
+            for len_dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+                for step in (1, 2):
+                    with self.subTest(bs=bs, gamma=gamma, dtype=len_dtype, step=step):
+                        draft = torch.arange(bs * gamma * step).reshape(
+                            bs, gamma * step
+                        )
+                        draft = (draft + 2**40).npu()[:, ::step]
+                        lengths = (
+                            (torch.arange(bs * step) // step % (gamma + 1))
+                            .to(len_dtype)
+                            .npu()[::step]
+                        )
+                        bonus = (torch.arange(bs * step) - 2**40).npu()[::step]
+                        inputs = {
+                            "draft_tokens": draft,
+                            "correct_len": lengths,
+                            "bonus": bonus,
+                            "verify_num_draft_tokens": gamma + 1,
+                            "gamma": gamma,
+                        }
+                        reference = dict(
+                            inputs,
+                            draft_tokens=draft.cpu(),
+                            correct_len=lengths.cpu(),
+                            bonus=bonus.cpu(),
+                        )
+                        expected = BuildOutTokens.torch(**reference)
+                        with mock.patch.object(
+                            sample,
+                            "build_out_tokens_triton",
+                            wraps=sample.build_out_tokens_triton,
+                        ) as kernel:
+                            actual = BuildOutTokens.execute(**inputs)
+                        kernel.assert_called_once_with(**inputs)
+                        self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, torch.int64)
+                        self.assertEqual(actual.device, draft.device)
+                        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual.cpu(), expected))
+
+    def test_placement_uses_first_tensor(self):
+        cpu = torch.zeros(1)
+        npu = cpu.npu()
+        self.assertFalse(inputs_on_cuda(None, cpu, npu))
+        self.assertTrue(inputs_on_cuda(None, npu, cpu))
+        with self.assertRaises(AssertionError):
+            inputs_on_cuda(1, flag=True)
+
+    def test_markov_greedy_matches_native_rounding(self):
+        for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            base = torch.randn(3, 4097, device="npu", dtype=dtype)
+            embeds = torch.randn(3, 33, device="npu", dtype=dtype)
+            weight = torch.randn(4097, 33, device="npu", dtype=dtype)
+            expected = (base + torch.nn.functional.linear(embeds, weight)).argmax(-1)
+            actual = MarkovGreedyStep.execute(
+                base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=weight
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, expected))
+
+    def test_argmax_and_accept_match_torch(self):
+        rows, block, vocab = 9, 7, 4097
+        logits = torch.randn(rows * block, vocab, device="npu")
+        logits[0, 5] = float("nan")
+        expected_top1 = logits.cpu().argmax(-1)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_row_argmax(logits).cpu(), expected_top1))
+        predict = expected_top1.reshape(rows, block)
+        candidates = predict.clone()
+        candidates[:, 1:] = predict[:, :-1]
+        for row in range(rows):
+            if row % block < block - 1:
+                col = row % block
+                candidates[row, col + 1] = (predict[row, col] + 1) % vocab
+        lengths = (candidates[:, 1:] == predict[:, :-1]).int().cumprod(1).sum(1)
+        bonus = predict[torch.arange(rows), lengths]
+        npu_candidates = candidates.npu()
+        integrated = AcceptGreedy.execute(
+            candidates=npu_candidates,
+            target_logits=logits,
+            verify_num_draft_tokens=block,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(integrated[0].dtype, torch.int32)
+        self.assertEqual(integrated[1].dtype, torch.int64)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(integrated[0].cpu(), lengths.int()))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(integrated[1].cpu(), bonus))
+
+    def test_softmax_temperature_mapping(self):
+        logits = torch.randn(9, 4097, device="npu")
+        temperatures = torch.tensor([0.3, 0.7, 1.2], device="npu")
+        actual = SoftmaxTemp.execute(
+            logits=logits, temperatures=temperatures, rows_per_request=3
+        )
+        expected = torch.softmax(
+            logits.cpu() / temperatures.cpu().repeat_interleave(3)[:, None], -1
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual.cpu(), expected, rtol=3e-5, atol=1e-7)
+
+    def test_cpu_reference_stays_available(self):
+        logits = torch.randn(6, 257)
+        temperatures = torch.tensor([0.7, 1.3])
+        expected = torch.softmax(
+            logits / temperatures.repeat_interleave(3)[:, None], -1
+        )
+        actual = SoftmaxTemp.execute(
+            logits=logits, temperatures=temperatures, rows_per_request=3
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, expected))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

The NVIDIA and NPU failures appear to come from dependencies in the CI snapshot:

- NVIDIA: test_gdn_prefill_graph.py fails during setup because it calls KVLayerRouter.from_layer_maps(pool, ()). The version used by this CI run accesses layer_maps[0][0] without checking whether the sequence is empty, causing an IndexError. This exact issue was fixed in [#47127](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47127) and has been merged into main.
- NPU: test_dspark_npu_dispatch.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sgl_kernel_npu.operators'. The CI run installs the 2026.9.0.post10 release. [#47217](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47217), which updates the CI dependency to 2026.9.0.post12, has been merged into main. The post12 A3 wheel contains the required operators/sample files, but this PR’s NPU CI still needs to be run with that version to confirm the fix
